pageCache.text:
PSHE - RSE - Health & Wellbeing
Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) at Gravesend Grammar School aims to provide students with the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to manage their lives, now and in the future.
We aim to provide students with the understanding they need to lead confident, healthy independent lives and to become informed, active and responsible citizens.
We believe the high-quality PSHE curriculum at GGS enables students to:
We follow a bespoke, tailor-made, PSHE programme that was developed to serve the different stages and ages of pupils as they develop. In its development, we considered national, local and school priorities as well as making sure the curriculum meets the requirements of the new statutory Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education guidance for schools.
We also cover a range of other carefully chosen topics and themes which have a strong emphasis on safeguarding, including online safety, bullying, mental health and well-being and personal safety. Where relevant we use professional organisations to support our delivery; from support to develop lessons to running sessions and delivering assemblies. Our ‘spiral curriculum’ approach means that students meet and revisit key topics on a number of occasions, exploring themes in increasingly greater depth and in an age-appropriate manner, as they move up through the school.
PSHE Curriculm Outline
“My two sons often come home and tell us about their PSHE lessons. We are so impressed with the variety and relevance of the content, and how this is delivered.”
At Gravesend Grammar School, we are committed to supporting the mental health and well-being of our students and staff. We strive to provide a caring environment where everyone in the community can feel listened to and supported.
Supporting students’ mental well-being is taken seriously. We continue to improve our provision through staff training, student focused activities. We work together with other organisations that specialise in the mental and emotional well-being of children and adults (including We Are With You and our local Mind Charity among others). We ensure all students have access to PSHE lessons, assemblies and tutor times that cover aspects of social emotional and mental health awareness and learning. Alongside this provision, we have trained counsellors and run a variety of nurture groups for students. We have a Mental Health Lead Teacher, four staff that are trained in Mental Health First Aid and we are committed to the Educational Staff Wellbeing Charter.
We want to make sure that all of our students and our parents/carers feel confident in the knowledge that, should their child be experiencing any level of mental ill health, there is support available at GGS to manage this.
We also provide a tailor-made online student Mental Health advice and signposting website and an online ‘concern button’ so that students can easily refer themselves and get the support and advice they need. Students can also speak to any member of staff about their or their peers' mental health concerns and this will be dealt with but our support teams.

Careers
Career Guidance at Gravesend Grammar School
The careers programme at GGS is designed to provide all students with the education, information, advice and guidance to help them make the right career decisions and is designed to meet the Gatsby Benchmarks.
The programme aims to raise aspirations and support students to achieve their full potential whilst they are in school and also in their future career paths.
All students have access to independent, impartial careers guidance from the school careers adviser who is qualified to level 7 and a member of the CDI professional register. They also benefit from a dedicated Careers team in School who have a breadth of experience and Careers Guidance qualifications.
In 2011, GGS was awarded the Investor in Careers award, a quality award which certifies that we have “achieved the most exacting standards of excellence in careers education and guidance.” The School is reassessed against the standards every three years and passed again in July 2022. The school is committed to upholding the standards of the Investor in Careers Award and is currently undergoing the reassessment process.
There is a focus on making all students aware of the opportunities that Higher Education has to offer. Strong links with local and Russell Group universities provide up to date information and the chance for students to experience at first hand a range of aspects of university life. All students are guided and supported through the UCAS application process via a series of activities including university visits, individual guidance and mock interviews.
Alongside activities relating to Higher Education are work-related learning activities, providing insight into career progression beyond education. Year 10 boys undertake a full week of work experience in a range of professions, both locally in the borough and further afield in Kent, Medway and central London. Links with local and larger corporate employers are utilised to raise awareness of the different routes into professions including apprenticeships in sectors such as accountancy, law, construction and engineering. Companies offering higher and degree level apprenticeships visit the school and seek out our school leavers.
Opportunities for the future are ever increasing and the process of finding your desired path can be confusing and stressful, but our expert team takes a pride in guiding you through this.
For further details of our careers programme and information for students, parents and employers please visit out dedicated careers site.
Careers leader – Mr J Berry, Head of Careers

Trust Choir Concert 2026: A Spectacular Start to ‘The Greatest Show’
On Tuesday 24th March 2026, Gravesend Grammar School proudly took part in night one of our Trust Choir Concert, themed ‘The Greatest Show’.
Our students delivered a lively and characterful performance of ‘Consider Yourself’ from Oliver!, capturing the spirit of the piece with confidence and enthusiasm. It was wonderful to see such strong stage presence and musicality on display.
Mr Mitchell also represented the school as part of the staff choir, joining colleagues from across the Trust for a fantastic Grease Megamix, which brought great energy and fun to the evening.
A highlight for all involved was the combined choir, where pupils from every school came together to perform A Million Dreams, Rewrite the Stars and This Is Me from The Greatest Showman. These moments truly reflected the unity and shared talent across our Trust.
We are incredibly proud of our students for their contribution to such a memorable evening and look forward to night two!

Drama
Drama at GGS offers a wide range of opportunities for students with varied talents from acting to technical, script writing and practitioner workshops.
All students whether they are an experienced performer or a complete novice, they are encouraged to join us to explore and develop their talents. There is something for everyone.
In our technical theatre club, students are able to explore the technical equipment we use for shows and performances; including lighting, sound set making and costume and makeup workshops led by industry professionals. During drama extracurricular sessions, students work on short performances, confidence building, comedy stretches and monologues and duologues. They have opportunities to share their own creations as well as working towards whole school productions and performances of well known and relevant playwrights.
Directing and producing workshops are provided to offer students the chance to develop their directing and production role skills, such as stage management, marketing and front of house. Students utilise these skills to run the whole school performances. Frequent trips to West End and local theatre performances serve to enhance students experience of live productions
Our GCSE students take on leadership roles in extra curricular activities and in the preparation of school productions.
They also have academic support sessions designed to improve exam preparation as well as exploring the analytical and evaluative skills of writing live theatre reviews and developing script writing skills.
We hold at least one major whole school live performance each year. In recent years, the School has put on ‘Little Shop of Horrors,’ ‘Bugsy Malone’, and ‘Avenue Q’. In addition to the performance of a play or musical, there are also regular showcases for example our ‘Shakespeare Shorts’ our ‘Drama festival’ and year group pantomime performances

Music
At Gravesend Grammar School we recognise the importance of musical education and the benefits it has on young developing minds.
We work to ensure that all students have access to exciting and engaging opportunities. Students are welcome to become part of our growing creative community, where we encourage all students to become involved in music in some way, as an enjoyable experience that supports academic and social development, as well as promoting good mental health.
Music is both a focus for study and a means of communal expression with students developing musical understanding and skills (in perception, as composers, and as performers) in classes, in option groups, individually and in school ensembles. Many celebrations of school life, such as assemblies, Prize Giving events and the Carol Service, are enhanced by musical performance. Additionally, we host our own music gigs and recitals throughout the school year, plus opportunities in collaboration with other local schools and organisations.
Participation and performance extend beyond the classroom.
Vocal and instrumental lessons are available to students in all year groups. A wide range of extra-curricular musical activities (instrumental groups, bands and a choir) take place each week during lunch time and after school. We strongly believe that the musical opportunities and experiences we provide serve as an ideal opportunity for students to develop important social skills, gain confidence and independence and friendships that will last a lifetime.

National Careers Week 2026
This week is the nationwide National Careers Week (NCW) from Monday 2nd March to Friday 6th March! This is about bringing together students, local employers and staff through careers events and activities.
At Gravesend Grammar School, we have a range of events and activities taking place throughout the week.
We also have an interactive Student Toolkit that is available here: https://view.genially.com/699e11dbcf6f08ba8afadd6c/interactive-content-ggs-ncw-student-toolkit.
The interactive Student Toolkit is a “go to” place for guidance and support based on where you are at, as a Key Stage 3, 4 or 5 student, in the school careers programme. There are a variety of resources in the student toolkit that can be accessed at home and at school. Each resource is tailored to one of the six learning areas which are central to development and growth.
Please delve into this and feel free to find out more about some of the aspects which you may have seen/heard of in the first part of this academic year.
If there are any queries at all, please do not hesitate to contact your Form Tutor and/or the Careers Team at careersteam@gravesendgrammar.com

Examination Results
GCSE Exam Results 2025
Year 11 students at Gravesend Grammar School celebrated a good year of results. Our overall Attainment 8 score was in the 5th percentile nationally.
44% of all grades were awarded at a 7-9 level whilst 24% were awarded at 8-9 highlighting a high percentage of top end levels achieved at GGS. 60% of all grades in Mathematics were awarded at the top 7-9 band, and 54% of those in English. Computer Science (69% 7+) and Physics (68% 7+) were also notably high performing subjects.
98% achieved a good pass in English and Mathematics, while 91% gained a strong pass in both subjects. We are pleased in the current educational climate that 78% of our students passed their English Baccalaureate which contains a challenging and rigorous set of subjects. To achieve the Ebacc, students need to attain strong grades in English, Maths, Science, a Humanity and a Language.
The ‘Attainment 8’ measure, average pupil achievement across 8 qualifications, including English and maths and at least 3 other rigorous English Baccalaureate qualifications is 6.5.
With regards to individual performance, 14 pupils have attained an average level of an 8-9. 24 pupils got 7 or more 8s/9s and 59 pupils got 7 or more 7s which are all improvements upon 2024.

A Level Exam Results 2025
We are so proud of our students and the staff that supported them in achieving such a strong set of A level results this year. These results were our best in over 10 years and testament to our programme of improving progress at A level.
We are a community grammar school with an inclusive entry criteria and we value the whole student, not just exam results. Alongside these outstanding results which are well above national averages are a vast range of unmeasured soft skills, including increasing engagement in extra curricular sports, music and drama as well as the widest range of leadership roles we have ever had providing opportunities not only to our Sixth Form students but also to the younger members of our community.
We are very proud of the diverse group of students we had with us for the past two years who entered our Sixth Form predominantly from year 11 here at GGS, but with a significant number from other schools. The overwhelming majority of students have gone onto their first choice of university including an increase in success with both Oxbridge and Medical school applications.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Gravesend Grammar School - Est 1893.
I am very proud to be the Headteacher of Gravesend Grammar School. I have spent over 20 years at the School as a teacher and a leader and I am passionate that our traditional values are upheld in a modern context.
My own expectations for the School are very high and I believe that students achieve through respect, hard work, friendship and exploration. These core values will be at the heart of everything that we do to ensure the very high academic standards continue. Our academic achievements are exceptionally high at both GCSE and A-level creating a gateway to the next steps for our students. The next step is usually University although we are seeing increasing numbers of students taking degree apprenticeship pathways.
Whilst the primary focus is to achieve high academic standards, I believe that a broad and rich curriculum is essential in creating well rounded individuals who can confidently take on the next phase of their lives, and which provides a balance to the demands of a rigorous academic curriculum.
My mission is a relatively simple one in that we must do everything we can to ensure that all our students make progress that enables them to be successful in later life. We also provide clear opportunities for teachers and support staff to excel and for all to continue to develop within their field.
As a selective school we are fortunate to be educating students who have high aspirations and have a strong commitment and loyalty to the School. In return, we provide a high quality learning environment with opportunities and challenges for all of our students both within and beyond the curriculum.
Malcolm Moaby BEd (Hons)

pageCache.text:
Our House System
The present House system was introduced in 1926 (before then there had been the Goths and Vikings, and the Saxons for the Junior Technical School). The stained glass windows for each House in the Library were produced for the opening of the new school when it moved to its present site in 1938. Therefore there are only windows for the four original Houses.
Cliff
Blue tie and sports shirts – students from the west of the Borough.
The stained glass window in the Library reflects the cement, paper and barge industries, plus references to the Roman camp at Springhead and to St John Franklin who sailed from Greenhithe on his last voyage. It includes the quote from Franklin, “I have been prompted to venture by an imperious sense of duty.” The name is derived from Overcliffe.
Downs
Yellow tie and sports shirts – students from the south of the Borough.
The stained glass window in the Library reflects the old Kent countryside, the Pilgrims’ Way and Geoffrey Chaucer, including the quote from Chaucer, “Truth is the highest thing to keep.”
Hill
Green tie and sports shirts – students from the east of the Borough.
The stained glass window in the Library reflects Windmill Hill and Gad’s Hill, with Charles Dickens. It includes the quote from Dickens, “A man in any station can do his duty.”
Town
Red tie and sports shirts – students from the centre of the Borough.
The stained glass window in the Library reflects the shipping industries and Gravesend as the gateway to the Port of London, with General Gordon. It includes the quote from Gordon, “Self is the best officer to do anything for you.”
School
Purple tie and sports shirts – students living in close proximity to the School.
In 1992, after many years of students not attending the School until they were 13, the School started to take students in after the 11+. The Year 7 intake consisted of five forms rather than four and School House came into being.
Fleet
White tie and sports shirts – name decided after consultation with both students and staff.
In 2012 the Year 7 intake went from 5 forms to 6 and another new House was introduced, Fleet.
The River Fleet rises at Springhead and flows into the Thames at Northfleet Harbour. Although this continues the tradition of signifying an area near to the School, students are no longer allocated to Houses by the area in which they live.

Appeals
When a parent is informed of the decision to refuse their child a place at a school for which they have applied, they have the right to lodge an appeal. This is the case for admissions after national offers day (1st March) and for In-year admissions applications.
Parents wishing to lodge an appeal must set out the grounds for their appeal in writing using the school appeal form. Appeals must be submitted to the school within the following timeframes:
Appeals lodged after the deadlines will be heard at a later convening of the appeals panel.
Once appeals have been lodged the Appeals’ Administrator will provide appellants with a time and date for their appeal at least 10 days before the appeal is to be heard. Appeals will be heard within 30 days of the appeal being lodged, unless dependant on exam results, in which case the appeal will be within 30 days of confirmation of exam results.
Appeals for the normal admissions round, after national offer day, will be heard across a number of dates in May and June.
The Appeals Administrator will provide clear guidance on the requirements for collecting evidence for an appeal, the procedures followed during the appeal and the names and roles of the panel members. The School cannot guarantee that evidence presented will be returned, so it is advisable to submit copies of children’s work and achievements. All evidence should be submitted along with the Appeal Form (and ideally no later than 30th April 2026 for the September admissions round).
The appeals panel will decide whether to direct the school to offer your son a place and will write to you following the final appeal date to inform you of their decision. Please read the FAQs Appeals document to find out more.
Additional Information
For this admission round (September 2026) Gravesend Grammar School received 255 first preferences from parents seeking a place at the school and 643 total preferences, where the school is named anywhere on a child’s common application form. This means that the school is heavily oversubscribed. When considering whether to lodge an appeal against the refusal to offer a place or not, please consider the information in this document carefully.
Should you decide to seek an appeal, evidence to support your case is important, especially if you are trying to overturn the results of the 11+ and/or convince the Panel that your son should be given a place. With your Appeal Form, therefore, it would be helpful, and advised, to include, if possible, some or all of the following:
· Headteacher/Class Teacher letter of support
· recent assessments
· a copy of the Year 5 annual report
· details of any mitigating circumstances, which might explain underperformance in the Kent test (11+)
· tracking sheet, (optional but advised) which shows your child’s progress over time
Work samples are not required as the Panel will not be in a position to assess their validity or context. In addition, it is not necessary to provide numerous certificates of achievement.

Open Days
Open mornings for September 2027 entrants will be:
Thursday 15th October 2026 (encouraged for Year 5 pupils)
Friday 16th October 2026 (encouraged for Year 6 pupils)
Click here to book your slot - booking will open in early October and you won't be able to use this link until then.
Please note that Kent Assessment decisions will be sent to parents email addresses after 4pm on Thursday 15th October 2026. The deadline for submissions of Secondary Application forms to the local authority is 2nd November 2026.
Open mornings are an opportunity to visit Gravesend Grammar School in order to help inform decisions about potential applications for a place
Visitors will be taken on a guided tour of the school by members of the existing student body, where they will be able to witness teaching and learning happening as it does on every other day of the year. Open mornings are also an opportunity to sample the atmosphere, as well as view the facilities the school has to offer . At the culmination of the tour there will be an address by the Head Teacher and Admissions Manager outlining the ethos and what parents should expect if they choose to send their sons to Gravesend Grammar School in year 7.
Throughout the morning staff will be available to answer any questions about the school or specific situations relating to your sons’, including the admissions process.
Sixth Form Open Evening
We would be delighted for year 11 students, and their parents to join us for our Sixth Form open evening.
Thursday 21st January 2027 - 6-8pm - no booking required.
You will be able to find out more about the A Level subjects you are interested in, speak to current students, subject leaders, the Sixth form team and careers guidance professionals. There will be a talk in the main hall from the Head Teacher and the Head of Sixth form, individual subject talks will take place throughout the evening.
